title: AI chat assistant detected
question: Does the site load an AI chat assistant whose users must be told they are talking to a machine?
method: Review when the static HTML of the home page loads a known chat or AI assistant (Intercom, Zendesk, Gorgias, Tidio, Drift, LivePerson, Ada, Crisp, Shopify Inbox and the like), and name it. Found (none detected) otherwise. The scan cannot tell whether the widget answers with AI. The disclosure appears inside the widget after JavaScript runs and cannot be checked. The duty often rests with the vendor that provides the AI system.

title: Machine-readable reservation of text and data mining
question: Does the store reserve text and data mining in a form machines can read, without shutting out search and shopping agents?
method: Look for a machine-readable reservation: robots.txt keeps at least one AI training crawler (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and the like) out of the whole site, robots.txt has Content-Usage lines, /.well-known/tdmrep.json is valid, or a tdm-reservation header or meta tag is set to 1. Also read the terms for reservation wording. Found when a machine-readable reservation exists and robots.txt still lets the core and major-assistant search crawlers of check A2.2 that fetch pages ({{crawlers:index.core}}, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and the like) read the first sampled product page. Google-Extended is a training reservation here, although Google also uses it for grounding in Gemini Apps, which A2.2 reports. Review when the reservation also blocks one of those search crawlers, or when it is only in the terms (not machine-readable under the 2025 Hamburg ruling). Found with a note when nothing is reserved, because reserving is a right, not a duty.

title: AI-generated product images marked
question: When product images carry AI-generation metadata, is it intact?
method: Fetch the main image of up to two sampled product pages (at most 2 MB each) and look in the file for the IPTC digital source type trainedAlgorithmicMedia or compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia, or a C2PA ai_generated or actions entry. Found when an image carries one of these markers. Otherwise the check does not apply: missing metadata does not show an image is camera-made, because CDNs often strip it.
